$comment: Utility withheld from mini-apps because of the mobile app lifecycle. Rendered as the ledger table in docs/mobile-lifecycle.md and enforced by conformance/doc-audit/mobile-lifecycle.test.mjs. Read docs/mobile-lifecycle.md before editing.

causes.os: The mobile OS forbids it. Nothing this repository can build changes the answer; only an OS capability, an entitlement, or a different host would.
causes.os-derived: The OS forbids something adjacent, and this is our implementation of living within it. A different implementation could recover part of the utility.
causes.self-imposed: Nothing in the mobile OS requires this. The platform chose it, and the cost to mini-apps is ours to remove.

forbiddenClaims.why: It is not a design choice. The OS suspends the host process; it does not limit how many sandboxes a running host may hold.

forbiddenClaims.pattern: One foreground mini-app at a time in v1, by design
forbiddenClaims.why: Same claim in a different sentence. Concurrent mini-apps have shipped; do not revive the single-slot limit as design.

forbiddenClaims.pattern: no background execution or ambient APIs, by design
forbiddenClaims.why: Background execution is an OS limit on iOS only; on Android it is ours. Attributing both to design hides the Android half. See MLC-BACKGROUND-ANDROID.

rows.utility: Mini-app code running while the host app is backgrounded on iOS
rows.decision: Backgrounding is a state transition: the worklet gets `suspend-node`, quiesces interfaces, and no mini-app executes
rows.cost: Nothing happens while the user is elsewhere: no sync, no delivery, no timers
rows.unlock: An iOS background execution mode for general network daemons. None exists; the declared `fetch` and `processing` modes are host sync budgets, not general execution
rows.note: iOS has no foreground-service equivalent. Re-check when Apple changes background execution policy or when H13 device measurements land.

rows.utility: A phone carrying transport, seeding, or propagation for other peers
rows.decision: Always-on roles default on for desktop and headless peers and are not promised on mobile
rows.cost: Peer density depends on desktop peers; a mini-app cannot assume its messages move while the phone sleeps
rows.unlock: Nothing an app can do. Android foreground-service peers narrow the gap; iOS does not close it
rows.note: This is the load-bearing reason desktop hosts exist as always-on peers at all.
